title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Remark 1's argument needs two unstated hypotheses: G^natural is normal in G^+, and G^+ is topologically generated by rho and sigma. Only then does u(x) congruent to x on generators propagate to all x.

For the general Z''' (sign eps different from 1), the congruences u(rho) congruent to rho^eps and u(sigma) congruent to sigma^eps do not by themselves give stability of G^natural, nor trivial action on G^+/G^natural. Grothendieck's own marginal note 'c'est mauvais' records this, so condition (4)d) must be kept as an axiom.
In (24) the machine transcription writes xi_3 gamma; it should be eps_3 gamma.

ideas.what: Group of automorphisms of a profinite triangle/modular-type group preserving the conjugacy classes of the generators up to sign, normalised at the cusp (u(epsilon_0) = epsilon_0^mu), modulo inner automorphisms by the cusp group
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group (GT or its genus-one/modular analogues); groups of 'special' or 'braid-like' outer automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; for genus 1 and the modular group: Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the GT idea; this explicit set-up is not published

ideas.what: Index-2 and index-4 subgroups as kernels of the sign characters eps_2, eps_3, eps_2*eps_3

ideas.modern_name: complex conjugation element in GT / Gal(Q-bar/Q)

ideas.what: Semidirect product Z ⋉ G^+ divided by the anti-diagonal image of the cusp group, giving an extension 1 -> G^+ -> G_{rho,sigma} -> Gamma -> 1
ideas.modern_name: extension associated with an outer action at a tangential base point (holomorph modulo inner part)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical group theory; arithmetic use by Ihara, Nakamura and others

ideas.what: Using conjugacy only by a normal 'level' subgroup G^natural rather than by the whole group
ideas.modern_name: GT-type groups attached to level structures or congruence subgroups
ideas.usually_credited_to: later work on level-structure versions of GT (e.g. Boggi, Enriquez's elliptic/cyclotomic GT); unsure of exact attribution

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up GT-type groups in which conjugacy of the generators is required only modulo a normal 'level' subgroup G^natural. He notices that the stability condition (4)d) is not automatic and must be kept. This amounts to an early level-structure variant of GT, but the page itself is mostly routine set-up.
missed.quote: c'est mauvais — on ne peut pas exiger ... (4) d) ... n'implique pas trivialité de G^+/G^natural
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Level-structure and congruence variants of GT are studied today, for example by Enriquez (cyclotomic and elliptic GT) and Boggi. Grothendieck's treatment, with G^natural-conjugacy and sign characters, may be of historical interest as a precursor, though it is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping in a GT-type construction: index-2 sign kernels, the complex-conjugation element, and the semidirect product modulo the cusp. Historically interesting as part of Grothendieck's own unpublished GT development, including a level-subgroup variant. But nothing on the page would surprise a specialist mathematically.
transcription_corrections: Line (24): gamma', gamma'', gamma''', gamma^0 should be the capital Gamma'_{rho,sigma} etc.; 'xi_3 gamma' should be eps_3 gamma.
'Ce sont donc des sous-groupes d'indice 2, 2, 2 [?] ou quotient' likely reads 'sous-groupes d'indice 1 ou 2 de Gamma_{rho,sigma} resp. Z_{rho,sigma} — d'indice ≤ 4 pour Gamma^0, Z^0'.
The left label '(1 Sigma_rho, gamma')' is probably the equation number '(25)' (cf. the following '(25bis)').
Throughout, hat G is the fraktur 𝔊 (𝔊^+, 𝔊^natural), not a hatted G.

The marginal formula reads approximately: 'Plus généralement, Z'''_{rho,sigma} ≃ {(u,mu,eps) ∈ Aut(𝔊^+) × hat Z^* × mu | a) u(rho) 𝔊^natural-conj. à rho^eps, b) u(sigma) 𝔊^natural-conj. à sigma^eps, c) u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu}'.
(28): l -> i_{L0,Z}(l)·l^{-1}; the arrow label is i^natural_{L0,G}.
